steps: Form a flat hand with your dominant hand, holding the fingers together and the thumb tucked in.
Hold your non-dominant hand in an open-B shape, flat and steady in front of you.
Tap your dominant flat hand twice against the midpoint between the non-dominant hand's thumb and fingertips.
Keep the non-dominant hand completely still while the dominant hand does the tapping.
Stay neutral-faced; the meaning comes from the double tap at the center, not from expression.
tip: Think of landing exactly halfway between the thumb and the fingertips — the middle point is the average.

steps: Open your dominant hand into a five handshape with all fingers spread wide.
Bend only your middle finger forward at the knuckle, leaving the other fingers straight.
Touch the tip of that bent middle finger to the pinkie-side edge of your non-dominant hand.
Jab the edge with the middle-finger tip in a short repeated motion, like pecking at the hand's edge.
Keep your face neutral; the emphasis stays on the repeated jab.
tip: One sign covers TECHNICAL, METHOD, and TECHNOLOGY — picture the middle finger tapping out the 'technique'.

steps: Make an S handshape with your non-dominant hand, fingers curled tight with the thumb wrapped over them.
Turn that S hand palm-down and hold it steady in front of you.
Form an I handshape with your dominant hand, raising the pinkie upward.
Rest the dominant I hand on the back of the palm-down S hand.
Move the I hand in two horizontal circles — clockwise or counter-clockwise, either is fine.
tip: The pinkie-finger hand circles on the closed S hand like a small island rising out of the water.

steps: Make a flat hand with your dominant hand, fingers held together.
Hold the flat hand a few inches in front of your head.
Bring the hand straight down in a single firm motion.
This means 'the front of' something — as in YOUR HOUSE, FRONT DOOR — not the directional IN-FRONT-OF.
tip: One straight downward stroke in front of your forehead marks the front side of a place or thing.
